item.title: Bose Levu Vakaturaga Bill an opportunity to correct past mistake and bring healing – Kamikamica
item.description: Kamikamica says the previous Government disrespected and derecognised the Bose Levu Vakaturaga, and the proposed legislation provides an opportunity to address this. He says the Bill would help return the Bose Levu Vakaturaga to what he describes as its rightful place in Fijian society.
item.content:encoded:
Kamikamica says the previous Government disrespected and derecognised the Bose Levu Vakaturaga, and the proposed legislation provides an opportunity to address this.

He says the Bill would help return the Bose Levu Vakaturaga to what he describes as its rightful place in Fijian society.

Cabinet has endorsed the start of a stand-alone legislative process to establish the Bose Levu Vakaturaga under the Constitution and in law.

The Ministry of iTaukei Affairs is required to carry out further consultations with relevant iTaukei institutions under the iTaukei Affairs Act 1944, before the Bill returns to Cabinet for final consideration and introduction in Parliament.

item.title: Water supply arrives in drought-affected Batiki Island today
item.description: An emergency water operation is underway to assist communities on Batiki Island affected by water shortages while support for water supply operations for affected maritime communities in the Northern and Western divisions is being planned. The Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and National Disaster Risk Management says that through the Divisional Commissioner Eastern Office, it is working
item.content:encoded:
An emergency water operation is underway to assist communities on Batiki Island affected by water shortages while support for water supply operations for affected maritime communities in the Northern and Western divisions is being planned.

The Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and National Disaster Risk Management says that through the Divisional Commissioner Eastern Office, it is working with the Ministry of Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport and the Water Authority of Fiji (WAF) to deliver emergency water supplies to the island.

The vessel MLC Vatulawa departed Narayan Jetty at 8.45pm last night and arrives in Batiki this morning.

The Ministry says the team will deliver emergency water supplies and assess alternative water sources on the island, while supporting communities that rely primarily on rainwater harvesting.

They says upon arrival, the team will establish the operation and begin distributing water, with priority given to the school and health centre.

The Ministry says a second phase of the operation is planned for tomorrow, following the team's return to Levuka to replenish water supplies.

They say as part of the wider response to drought-affected communities, the Ministry and the Ministry of Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport will also work together to coordinate and support water supply operations for affected maritime communities in the Northern and Western divisions.

The Ministry says they will continue to monitor the evolving impacts of El Niño and work with stakeholders to ensure the Government's response is coordinated and timely assistance is provided to affected communities.

item.title: Young people must be part of decision-making – Kamikamica
item.description: Speaking at the International Day of Peace Youth Peace Forum at the University of the South Pacific's Pasifika Campus in Nasese , Kamikamica says young people are not only Fiji's future but are already playing an important role in the country. He says meaningful youth participation should go beyond listening to young people and should provide them with opportunities, to contribute to the developme
item.content:encoded:
Speaking at the International Day of Peace Youth Peace Forum at the University of the South Pacific's Pasifika Campus in Nasese , Kamikamica says young people are not only Fiji's future but are already playing an important role in the country.

He says meaningful youth participation should go beyond listening to young people and should provide them with opportunities, to contribute to the development of policies and take on responsibilities.

Kamikamica says peace is also about whether people feel safe, have access to education and jobs, and can afford food.

He says it is also about whether people can seek help for issues such as HIV and drugs without shame.

Kamikamica says Fiji's young people are growing up at a time when artificial intelligence, technology, social media, climate change and global developments are rapidly changing the world.

He also highlighted the impact of drugs on young people, saying drug use can damage their health, education and families.

Kamikamica says prevention, education, counselling and health services need to be available, while young people should also be involved in developing solutions to these problems.

He also encouraged young people to take part in discussions about Fiji's Constitution, saying they should understand their rights and responsibilities and how the country's institutions work.

Kamikamica says creating opportunities for young people is also important for peace.

He says this includes helping young people enter agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and digital businesses, and supporting them to create jobs rather than only look for employment.

Kamikamica challenged young people to learn and participate in their communities.

He also encouraged them to protect one another, including protecting their friends from drugs and supporting people living with HIV.
